sanskrit: so 'vardhata divaṃ stabdhvā sūryavaiśvānaropamaḥ kiṃ karomīti covāca kālasūrya ivoditaḥ śakraṃ jahīti cāpy ukto jagāma tridivaṃ tataḥ
english: He grew, propping up the sky, blazing like the sun and fire together. Rising like the sun of doom, he said: 'What shall I do?' And when told 'Kill Indra,' he set off for the highest heaven.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavad vṛtravāsavayos tadā saṃkruddhayor mahāghoraṃ prasaktaṃ kurusattama
english: Then a fierce and terrible battle broke out between Vṛtra and Vāsava — both enraged — that continued without pause, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato jagrāha devendraṃ vṛtro vīraḥ śatakratum apāvṛtya sa jagrāsa vṛtraḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ
english: Then the mighty Vṛtra seized the lord of gods, the hundred-sacrificed Śakra; opening wide, Vṛtra swallowed him in rage.

sanskrit: graste vṛtreṇa śakre tu saṃbhrāntās tridaśās tadā asṛjaṃs te mahāsattvā jṛmbhikāṃ vṛtranāśinīm
english: When Śakra had been swallowed by Vṛtra, the gods were seized with panic; those great beings then emitted the yawning power that would destroy Vṛtra.

sanskrit: vijṛmbhamāṇasya tato vṛtrasyāsyād apāvṛtāt svāny aṅgāny abhisaṃkṣipya niṣkrānto balasūdanaḥ tataḥ prabhṛti lokeṣu jṛmbhikā prāṇisaṃśritā
english: As Vṛtra yawned and his mouth gaped open, the slayer of Bala contracted his own limbs and slipped out. From that time onward, the yawn has dwelt among living creatures in the world.

sanskrit: jahṛṣuś ca surāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā śakraṃ viniḥsṛtam tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ vṛtravāsavayoḥ punaḥ saṃrabdhayos tadā ghoraṃ suciraṃ bharatarṣabha
english: All the gods rejoiced on seeing Śakra come out. Then the terrible battle between Vṛtra and Vāsava began again, both furious, lasting a long while, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yadā vyavardhata raṇe vṛtro balasamanvitaḥ tvaṣṭus tapobalād vidvāṃs tadā śakro nyavartata
english: When Vṛtra, empowered by the strength of Tvaṣṭṛ's austerities, grew mightier in battle, the wise Śakra then turned back.

sanskrit: nivṛtte tu tadā devā viṣādam agaman param sametya śakreṇa ca te tvaṣṭus tejovimohitāḥ amantrayanta te sarve munibhiḥ saha bhārata
english: When he retreated, the gods fell into deep despair. Coming together with Śakra, bewildered by the power of Tvaṣṭṛ, they all took counsel with the sages, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryam iti te rājan vicintya bhayamohitāḥ jagmuḥ sarve mahātmānaṃ manobhir viṣṇum avyayam upaviṣṭā mandarāgre sarve vṛtravadhepsavaḥ
english: Deliberating on what must be done, O king, and bewildered by fear, they all went in their minds to the imperishable great-souled Viṣṇu; they all gathered on the peak of Mandara, all desiring the slaying of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: indra uvāca sarvaṃ vyāptam idaṃ devā vṛtreṇa jagad avyayam na hy asya sadṛśaṃ kiṃ cit pratighātāya yad bhavet
english: Indra said: 'O gods, this entire imperishable world has been pervaded by Vṛtra. There is nothing comparable that could serve to oppose him.'

sanskrit: samartho hy abhavaṃ pūrvam asamartho 'smi sāṃpratam kathaṃ kuryāṃ nu bhadraṃ vo duṣpradharṣaḥ sa me mataḥ
english: 'Formerly I was capable; now I am not. How then can I secure your welfare? My view is that he is extremely difficult to overcome.'

sanskrit: tejasvī ca mahātmā ca yuddhe cāmitavikramaḥ graset tribhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam
english: 'He is radiant, great-souled, and of boundless might in battle; he could devour all three worlds together with gods, asuras, and men.'

sanskrit: tasmād viniścayam imaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ me divaukasaḥ viṣṇoḥ kṣayam upāgamya sametya ca mahātmanā tena saṃmantrya vetsyāmo vadhopāyaṃ durātmanaḥ
english: 'Therefore, O dwellers of heaven, hear this resolution of mine: let us go to the abode of Viṣṇu, meet with that great-souled one, and through counsel with him discover the means of slaying that evil being.'

sanskrit: śalya uvāca evam ukte maghavatā devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tadā śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ devaṃ jagmur viṣṇuṃ mahābalam
english: Śalya said: When Maghavat had spoken thus, the gods along with the hosts of sages went to Viṣṇu, the mighty god who is refuge for the refugeless.

sanskrit: ūcuś ca sarve deveśaṃ viṣṇuṃ vṛtrabhayārditāḥ tvayā lokās trayaḥ krāntās tribhir vikramaṇaiḥ prabho
english: Tormented by fear of Vṛtra, they all addressed Viṣṇu, lord of gods: 'O lord, you have traversed the three worlds with your three strides.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ cāhṛtaṃ viṣṇo daityāś ca nihatā raṇe baliṃ baddhvā mahādaityaṃ śakro devādhipaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: 'O Viṣṇu, you brought back the nectar of immortality, the daityas were slain in battle, and having bound the great daitya Bali, Śakra was made lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tvaṃ prabhuḥ sarvalokānāṃ tvayā sarvam idaṃ tatam tvaṃ hi deva mahādevaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ
english: 'You are the lord of all worlds; by you all this is pervaded. You, O god, are the great god, revered by all the worlds.

sanskrit: gatir bhava tvaṃ devānāṃ sendrāṇām amarottama jagad vyāptam idaṃ sarvaṃ vṛtreṇāsurasūdana
english: 'Be the refuge of the gods together with Indra, O best of immortals, O slayer of asuras. This entire world is pervaded by Vṛtra.'

sanskrit: viṣṇur uvāca avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ me bhavatāṃ hitam uttamam tasmād upāyaṃ vakṣyāmi yathāsau na bhaviṣyati
english: Viṣṇu said: 'I must certainly do what is supremely beneficial for you. Therefore I shall declare the means by which that one shall cease to exist.'

sanskrit: gacchadhvaṃ sarṣigandharvā yatrāsau viśvarūpadhṛk sāma tasya prayuñjadhvaṃ tata enaṃ vijeṣyatha
english: 'Go — sages and gandharvas — to where that bearer of the universal form dwells; employ conciliation toward him, and thereby you shall overcome him.'

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati gatir devāḥ śakrasya mama tejasā adṛśyaś ca pravekṣyāmi vajram asyāyudhottamam
english: 'O gods, I shall be Śakra's refuge through my own power. Becoming invisible, I shall enter the thunderbolt, that foremost of weapons, which he shall hurl.'

sanskrit: gacchadhvam ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ gandharvaiś ca surottamāḥ vṛtrasya saha śakreṇa saṃdhiṃ kuruta māciram
english: 'Go, O best of gods, together with the sages and gandharvas; without delay, make peace between Vṛtra and Śakra.'

sanskrit: śalya uvāca evam uktās tu devena ṛṣayas tridaśās tathā yayuḥ sametya sahitāḥ śakraṃ kṛtvā puraḥsaram
english: Śalya said: Thus addressed by the god, the sages and the thirty gods went together, placing Śakra in the lead.

sanskrit: samīpam etya ca tadā sarva eva mahaujasaḥ taṃ tejasā prajvalitaṃ pratapantaṃ diśo daśa
english: Drawing near, all of them, mighty in splendour, beheld that one blazing with radiance and scorching the ten directions —

sanskrit: grasantam iva lokāṃs trīn sūryācandramasau yathā dadṛśus tatra te vṛtraṃ śakreṇa saha devatāḥ
english: — as though swallowing the three worlds, like the sun and the moon. The gods, along with Śakra, saw Vṛtra there.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo 'tha tato 'bhyetya vṛtram ūcuḥ priyaṃ vacaḥ vyāptaṃ jagad idaṃ sarvaṃ tejasā tava durjaya
english: Then the sages approached Vṛtra and spoke pleasing words: 'O unconquerable one, this entire world is pervaded by your splendour.

sanskrit: na ca śaknoṣi nirjetuṃ vāsavaṃ bhūrivikramam yudhyatoś cāpi vāṃ kālo vyatītaḥ sumahān iha
english: 'Yet you have not been able to conquer Vāsava, who is of vast might; and a very great time has passed here while the two of you have fought.

sanskrit: pīḍyante ca prajāḥ sarvāḥ sadevāsuramānavāḥ sakhyaṃ bhavatu te vṛtra śakreṇa saha nityadā avāpsyasi sukhaṃ tvaṃ ca śakralokāṃś ca śāśvatān
english: 'All living creatures are tormented — gods, asuras, and men alike. O Vṛtra, let friendship be established between you and Śakra forever. You shall obtain happiness and the eternal worlds of Śakra.'

sanskrit: ṛṣivākyaṃ niśamyātha sa vṛtraḥ sumahābalaḥ uvāca tāṃs tadā sarvān praṇamya śirasāsuraḥ
english: Having heard the words of the sages, that extremely powerful Vṛtra, the asura, bowed his head to them all and then spoke:

sanskrit: sarve yūyaṃ mahābhāgā gandharvāś caiva sarvaśaḥ yad brūta tac chrutaṃ sarvaṃ mamāpi śṛṇutānaghāḥ
english: 'You are all of great fortune, and the gandharvas as well in every respect. All that you say has been heard by me. Now hear me also, O sinless ones.

sanskrit: saṃdhiḥ kathaṃ vai bhavitā mama śakrasya cobhayoḥ tejasor hi dvayor devāḥ sakhyaṃ vai bhavitā katham
english: 'How can there ever be peace between me and Śakra? How, O gods, can friendship come to pass between two such forces of power?'

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ sakṛt satāṃ saṃgataṃ lipsitavyaṃ; tataḥ paraṃ bhavitā bhavyam eva nātikramet satpuruṣeṇa saṃgataṃ; tasmāt satāṃ saṃgataṃ lipsitavyam
english: The sages said: 'Fellowship with the good is to be sought even once; whatever is to be thereafter will be as it must be. One should not overstep fellowship with good men. Therefore fellowship with the good is always to be sought.'

sanskrit: dṛḍhaṃ satāṃ saṃgataṃ cāpi nityaṃ; brūyāc cārthaṃ hy arthakṛcchreṣu dhīraḥ mahārthavat satpuruṣeṇa saṃgataṃ; tasmāt santaṃ na jighāṃseta dhīraḥ
english: 'Fellowship with the good is firm and ever enduring; the wise man speaks truth in difficult situations of meaning. Fellowship with a good person is of great significance. Therefore a wise man should not seek to harm the virtuous.'

sanskrit: indraḥ satāṃ saṃmataś ca nivāsaś ca mahātmanām satyavādī hy adīnaś ca dharmavit suviniścitaḥ
english: 'Indra is honoured by the virtuous and is the abode of great souls; he is a speaker of truth, undepressed, a knower of righteousness, and ever resolute.'

sanskrit: tena te saha śakreṇa saṃdhir bhavatu śāśvataḥ evaṃ viśvāsam āgaccha mā te bhūd buddhir anyathā
english: 'Let there be with him — with Śakra — an everlasting peace. Come to this trust; let your mind not be otherwise disposed.'

sanskrit: śalya uvāca maharṣivacanaṃ śrutvā tān uvāca mahādyutiḥ avaśyaṃ bhagavanto me mānanīyās tapasvinaḥ
english: Śalya said: Hearing the words of the great sages, the one of great splendour addressed them: 'Certainly, O blessed ones, the ascetics are to be honoured by me.

sanskrit: bravīmi yad ahaṃ devās tat sarvaṃ kriyatām iha tataḥ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi yad ūcur māṃ dvijarṣabhāḥ
english: 'O gods, let all that I say be done here; and I shall do all that the foremost of twice-born have said to me.'

sanskrit: na śuṣkeṇa na cārdreṇa nāśmanā na ca dāruṇā na śastreṇa na vajreṇa na divā na tathā niśi
english: 'Not by that which is dry, not by that which is wet, not by stone, not by wood, not by weapon, not by the thunderbolt, not by day, and not by night —

sanskrit: vadhyo bhaveyaṃ viprendrāḥ śakrasya saha daivataiḥ evaṃ me rocate saṃdhiḥ śakreṇa saha nityadā
english: '— under these conditions may I be slain by Śakra together with the gods, O foremost of brahmins. Such a peace with Śakra pleases me forever.'

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva ṛṣayas tam ūcur bharatarṣabha evaṃ kṛte tu saṃdhāne vṛtraḥ pramudito 'bhavat
english: 'So be it,' the sages said to him, O bull of the Bhāratas. With peace thus established, Vṛtra became joyful.

sanskrit: yattaḥ sadābhavac cāpi śakro 'marṣasamanvitaḥ vṛtrasya vadhasaṃyuktān upāyān anucintayan randhrānveṣī samudvignaḥ sadābhūd balavṛtrahā
english: But Śakra, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, was ever vigilant and filled with resentment, constantly thinking of means for killing Vṛtra, perpetually anxious and watching for an opening.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit samudrānte tam apaśyan mahāsuram saṃdhyākāla upāvṛtte muhūrte ramyadāruṇe
english: Once he saw that great asura at the ocean's edge at the time of twilight, that moment both beautiful and dreadful.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcintya bhagavān varadānaṃ mahātmanaḥ saṃdhyeyaṃ vartate raudrā na rātrir divasaṃ na ca vṛtraś cāvaśyavadhyo 'yaṃ mama sarvaharo ripuḥ
english: Then the blessed god reflected on the boon of the great-souled one: 'This is the fearful twilight — neither night nor day. And Vṛtra, this enemy who plunders everything, must certainly be killed by me.'

sanskrit: yadi vṛtraṃ na hanmy adya vañcayitvā mahāsuram mahābalaṃ mahākāyaṃ na me śreyo bhaviṣyati
english: 'If I do not slay Vṛtra today, having deceived this great asura of enormous strength and massive body, no good will come to me.'

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintayann eva śakro viṣṇum anusmaran atha phenaṃ tadāpaśyat samudre parvatopamam
english: Even as Śakra was thus deliberating and calling Viṣṇu to mind, he then saw in the ocean a mountain-like mass of foam.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ śuṣko na cārdro 'yaṃ na ca śastram idaṃ tathā enaṃ kṣepsyāmi vṛtrasya kṣaṇād eva naśiṣyati
english: 'This is neither dry nor wet, nor is it a weapon as such. I shall hurl this at Vṛtra — in an instant he shall perish.'

sanskrit: savajram atha phenaṃ taṃ kṣipraṃ vṛtre nisṛṣṭavān praviśya phenaṃ taṃ viṣṇur atha vṛtraṃ vyanāśayat
english: Then along with the thunderbolt he swiftly hurled that foam at Vṛtra; and Viṣṇu, having entered that foam, destroyed Vṛtra.

sanskrit: nihate tu tato vṛtre diśo vitimirābhavan pravavau ca śivo vāyuḥ prajāś ca jahṛṣus tadā
english: With Vṛtra slain, the directions became free of darkness, an auspicious wind blew, and all creatures rejoiced.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ ṛṣayaś ca mahendraṃ tam astuvan vividhaiḥ stavaiḥ
english: Then the gods together with gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents, and the sages too, praised great Indra with various hymns.

sanskrit: namaskṛtaḥ sarvabhūtaiḥ sarvabhūtāni sāntvayan hataśatruḥ prahṛṣṭātmā vāsavaḥ saha daivataiḥ viṣṇuṃ tribhuvanaśreṣṭhaṃ pūjayām āsa dharmavit
english: Saluted by all beings, soothing all beings, his enemy slain and his heart overjoyed, Vāsava, together with the gods, honoured Viṣṇu, the foremost of the three worlds — Vāsava, who knows righteousness.

sanskrit: tato hate mahāvīrye vṛtre devabhayaṃkare anṛtenābhibhūto 'bhūc chakraḥ paramadurmanāḥ traiśīrṣayābhibhūtaś ca sa pūrvaṃ brahmahatyayā
english: Then, after mighty Vṛtra, the terror of the gods, was slain, Śakra became overwhelmed by falsehood and utterly despondent — beset also by the guilt of the three-headed one, and by brahminicide from before.

sanskrit: so 'ntam āśritya lokānāṃ naṣṭasaṃjño vicetanaḥ na prājñāyata devendras tv abhibhūtaḥ svakalmaṣaiḥ praticchanno vasaty apsu ceṣṭamāna ivoragaḥ
english: Taking refuge at the edge of the worlds, bereft of consciousness and sense, the lord of gods could not be found, overwhelmed by his own sins; hidden away, he dwelt in the waters like a snake coiling within.

sanskrit: tataḥ pranaṣṭe devendre brahmahatyābhayārdite bhūmiḥ pradhvastasaṃkāśā nirvṛkṣā śuṣkakānanā vicchinnasrotaso nadyaḥ sarāṃsy anudakāni ca
english: Then, with the lord of gods gone and tormented by the dread of brahminicide, the earth appeared devastated — treeless, its forests withered, rivers with broken courses, and lakes without water.

sanskrit: saṃkṣobhaś cāpi sattvānām anāvṛṣṭikṛto 'bhavat devāś cāpi bhṛśaṃ trastās tathā sarve maharṣayaḥ
english: There was also a tumult among living beings caused by drought; the gods were greatly frightened, as were all the great sages.

sanskrit: arājakaṃ jagat sarvam abhibhūtam upadravaiḥ tato bhītābhavan devāḥ ko no rājā bhaved iti
english: The entire world, kingless, was overcome by calamities; and the gods became afraid, wondering: 'Who will be our king?'

sanskrit: divi devarṣayaś cāpi devarājavinākṛtāḥ na ca sma kaś cid devānāṃ rājyāya kurute manaḥ
english: In heaven, the divine sages too were bereft of their king of gods, and none among the gods turned their mind toward kingship.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca ṛṣayo 'thābruvan sarve devāś ca tridaśeśvarāḥ ayaṃ vai nahuṣaḥ śrīmān devarājye 'bhiṣicyatām te gatvāthābruvan sarve rājā no bhava pārthiva
english: Śalya said: Then all the sages and the gods, lords of the thirty, spoke: 'Let this glorious Nahuṣa be consecrated to the kingship of the gods.' They all went and said to him: 'Be our king, O lord of earth.'

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca nahuṣo devān ṛṣigaṇāṃs tathā pitṛbhiḥ sahitān rājan parīpsan hitam ātmanaḥ
english: Nahuṣa addressed those gods and the hosts of sages together with the ancestors, O king, seeking what was beneficial for himself:

sanskrit: durbalo 'haṃ na me śaktir bhavatāṃ paripālane balavāñ jāyate rājā balaṃ śakre hi nityadā
english: 'I am weak; I have not the strength to protect you. A king is born from strength, and strength ever resides in Śakra.'

sanskrit: tam abruvan punaḥ sarve devāḥ sarṣipurogamāḥ asmākaṃ tapasā yuktaḥ pāhi rājyaṃ triviṣṭape
english: All the gods, with the sages at their head, spoke to him again: 'Endowed with the power of our austerities, rule the kingdom in heaven.'

sanskrit: parasparabhayaṃ ghoram asmākaṃ hi na saṃśayaḥ abhiṣicyasva rājendra bhava rājā triviṣṭape
english: 'Without doubt a terrible mutual fear prevails among us. Be consecrated, O lord of kings; be king in heaven.'

sanskrit: devadānavayakṣāṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ tathā pitṛgandharvabhūtānāṃ cakṣurviṣayavartinām teja ādāsyase paśyan balavāṃś ca bhaviṣyasi
english: 'You shall absorb the energy of gods, dānavas, yakṣas, sages, rākṣasas, ancestors, gandharvas, and beings that fall within range of your sight — and thus you shall become powerful.'

sanskrit: dharmaṃ puraskṛtya sadā sarvalokādhipo bhava brahmarṣīṃś cāpi devāṃś ca gopāyasva triviṣṭape
english: 'Always placing righteousness foremost, be lord over all worlds. Protect the brahmin sages and the gods in heaven.'

sanskrit: sudurlabhaṃ varaṃ labdhvā prāpya rājyaṃ triviṣṭape dharmātmā satataṃ bhūtvā kāmātmā samapadyata
english: Having obtained that most rare boon and attained the kingship of heaven, having been virtuous of soul continually, he now became enslaved to desire.

sanskrit: devodyāneṣu sarveṣu nandanopavaneṣu ca kailāse himavatpṛṣṭhe mandare śvetaparvate sahye mahendre malaye samudreṣu saritsu ca
english: In all the divine gardens and in the groves of Nandana, on Kailāsa and the slope of the Himālayas, on Mandara, Śvetaparvata, Sahya, Mahendra, Malaya, in the oceans and in the rivers —

sanskrit: apsarobhiḥ parivṛto devakanyāsamāvṛtaḥ nahuṣo devarājaḥ san krīḍan bahuvidhaṃ tadā
english: — surrounded by apsarases and encircled by divine maidens, Nahuṣa, now king of the gods, sported in many ways.

sanskrit: śṛṇvan divyā bahuvidhāḥ kathāḥ śrutimanoharāḥ vāditrāṇi ca sarvāṇi gītaṃ ca madhurasvaram
english: He listened to various divine tales delightful to the ear, to all manner of musical instruments, and to singing with sweet voices.

sanskrit: viśvāvasur nāradaś ca gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ ca devendraṃ mūrtimanta upasthitāḥ mārutaḥ surabhir vāti manojñaḥ sukhaśītalaḥ
english: Viśvāvasu and Nārada, the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases, and the six seasons in bodily form attended upon the lord of gods; a fragrant, charming, cool and pleasant wind blew.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi krīḍatas tasya nahuṣasya mahātmanaḥ saṃprāptā darśanaṃ devī śakrasya mahiṣī priyā
english: While the great-souled Nahuṣa was thus sporting, there came into his sight the beloved queen of Śakra, the goddess.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ saṃdṛśya duṣṭātmā prāha sarvān sabhāsadaḥ indrasya mahiṣī devī kasmān māṃ nopatiṣṭhati
english: Seeing her, the corrupt-souled one said to all those in his assembly: 'Why does the divine queen of Indra not attend upon me?'

sanskrit: aham indro 'smi devānāṃ lokānāṃ ca tatheśvaraḥ āgacchatu śacī mahyaṃ kṣipram adya niveśanam
english: 'I am Indra of the gods, and likewise lord of the worlds; let Śacī come to my dwelling swiftly today.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā durmanā devī bṛhaspatim uvāca ha rakṣa māṃ nahuṣād brahmaṃs tavāsmi śaraṇaṃ gatā
english: Hearing this, the goddess, dejected in heart, said to Bṛhaspati: 'Protect me from Nahuṣa, O brahmin; I have come to you for refuge.'

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannāṃ brahmas tvaṃ māṃ prabhāṣase devarājasya dayitām atyantasukhabhāginīm
english: 'You address me, O brahmin, as one endowed with all auspicious marks, the beloved of the king of gods, partaker of supreme bliss,

sanskrit: avaidhavyena saṃyuktām ekapatnīṃ pativratām uktavān asi māṃ pūrvam ṛtāṃ tāṃ kuru vai giram
english: 'as one joined to a living husband, a devoted wife true to one husband. You have spoken words to me before — make those words true now.'

sanskrit: noktapūrvaṃ ca bhagavan mṛṣā te kiṃ cid īśvara tasmād etad bhavet satyaṃ tvayoktaṃ dvijasattama
english: 'Never before have you spoken anything false, O blessed lord. Therefore let what you have said to me come true, O best of twice-born.'

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir athovāca indrāṇīṃ bhayamohitām yad uktāsi mayā devi satyaṃ tad bhavitā dhruvam
english: Then Bṛhaspati said to Indrāṇī, bewildered by fear: 'What I have said to you, O goddess, will certainly come true.

sanskrit: drakṣyase devarājānam indraṃ śīghram ihāgatam na bhetavyaṃ ca nahuṣāt satyam etad bravīmi te samānayiṣye śakreṇa nacirād bhavatīm aham
english: 'You will see the king of gods, Indra, coming here soon. You need have no fear of Nahuṣa — this I truly tell you. I shall reunite you with Śakra before long.'

sanskrit: atha śuśrāva nahuṣa indrāṇīṃ śaraṇaṃ gatām bṛhaspater aṅgirasaś cukrodha sa nṛpas tadā
english: Then Nahuṣa heard that Indrāṇī had taken refuge with Bṛhaspati, son of Aṅgiras, and that king became enraged.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca kruddhaṃ tu nahuṣaṃ jñātvā devāḥ sarṣipurogamāḥ abruvan devarājānaṃ nahuṣaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Śalya said: Knowing Nahuṣa to be enraged, the gods, with the sages at their head, addressed Nahuṣa, king of the gods, terrible in aspect:

sanskrit: devarāja jahi krodhaṃ tvayi kruddhe jagadvibho trastaṃ sāsuragandharvaṃ sakiṃnaramahoragam
english: 'O king of gods, O lord of the world, abandon your anger. When you are enraged, the world is frightened — asuras, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and great serpents alike.'
